grh_fb683af1db2b1731a047.title: Visiting Lady
paragraphs: Rivers End goes overboard entertaining glamorous New York visitor Brenda Marsh, while Judy and the other townspeople exhaust themselves trying to prove how sophisticated the village can be. Brenda finally admits to Dr. Christian that she came to the country hoping to escape exactly this kind of social whirl and simply wants a chance to rest. During a drive, an out-of-control truck causes a serious crash that leaves Judy badly injured; Brenda keeps her head, gets Dr. Christian and Judy to help, and earns the town's respect as far more than an artificial society girl. Judy recovers, Roy's fright makes his feelings for her unmistakable, and Brenda's only remaining request is that Rivers End please stop giving parties for her.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, Gloria Holden, Beverly Brown, and Charles Lewis. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_fb13ab50a5fcc1fe3c73.title: The New Sheriff
paragraphs: Virtue City's sheriff election is being manipulated by gunman Gus Cotton to put his brother Roy in office, and Britt is reluctantly drafted as the neutral election official. The voters respond with an enormous write-in campaign for Britt himself, making him sheriff by a landslide and even electing him mayor. Because resigning would hand the sheriff's job to Roy, Britt temporarily accepts the office, names the Cotton brothers deputies, and invents a rumor that their old enemy Tracer McGinnest is approaching with a gang. Rather than serve in Britt's posse, the Cottons flee town, allowing Britt to resign and Ernie Needle to become sheriff.

grh_fbbd9ee570fee4b8dc05.title: Escape from Smoke Falls
paragraphs: When outlaw Falk shoots the Smoke Falls sheriff and escapes, Britt is asked to pursue him with only one local rider. He chooses the quiet Tom Lebrit over boastful Spud Hooker because Tom knows there is more to manhunting than fast shooting, while Spud races after Falk alone. Falk captures Spud and tries to use him as a human shield at a cave, but Tom tackles Spud out of the line of fire and is wounded as Britt brings Falk down. Tom admits he risked himself because Ellen, the girl both men care for, loves Spud.

grh_fb3473ccad51222fc0dc.title: My Country-A Poem of America
paragraphs: Russell Davenport adapts his own My Country: A Poem of America into a patriotic radio meditation on the nation's people, work, homes, history and democratic inheritance. Multiple voices celebrate farmers, builders, families and servicemen while also treating freedom as an obligation passed from earlier generations through those dying in the current war. The poem closes by arguing that American liberty cannot remain private or isolated: freedom must be shared so that the democratic promise defended at home can extend to people beyond America's borders.

The cast includes Anne Seymour, Martin Blain, Mason Adams, Marguerite Morrisey, and Berry Kroeger. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director and Russell Davenport as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.
